interpretation: Model-native contrast subspace, leave-one-scene-out (the subspace scoring scene i is fit on the other scenes' TRUE interactions only; cross-validated statistics in the sense of arXiv:2510.00845). [egg, per-token, k=4] raw cosine 0.40 -> projected 0.65 (sign-flip p 0.0002); controls: random subspace 0.36, action-main-effect subspace 0.45, quartet-shuffled subspace 0.65; capture 23% (random 0.4%); smallest principal angle to the action subspace 19 deg. Projected Rec H1 0.91 vs H0 0.78 vs H0' 0.83; specificity Rec_h1 - Rec_h0 = +0.081 (p 0.022), raw-space specificity -0.009 (p 0.61). [gripper_corridor, per-token, k=4] raw cosine 0.18 -> projected 0.23 (sign-flip p 0.0002); controls: random subspace 0.18, action-main-effect subspace 0.13, quartet-shuffled subspace 0.18; capture 18% (random 0.4%); smallest principal angle to the action subspace 14 deg. Projected Rec H1 1.00 vs H0 0.96 vs H0' 0.97; specificity Rec_h1 - Rec_h0 = +0.021 (p 0.55), raw-space specificity -0.020 (p 0.043). Reading guide: a random k-subspace reproduces the raw cosine (it neither helps nor hurts), so the gain over the random control is the coordinate-system effect; if the quartet-shuffled subspace scores as well as the interaction subspace, the shared directions are generic scene/action structure rather than an interaction-specific code. Pooled-feature Rec at small k has tiny denominators and is unstable; use per-token medians. k=1 projected cosine is a sign test (+-1 per scene). The specificity p (Rec_h1 - Rec_h0) is the number that says whether the model treats the on-path egg differently from the off-path egg; a large p means it does not, in raw or shared coordinates.
